request.user:
[2023 summer phd probability — problem 1]

Part I, Exercise 1. Let $(X_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a sequence of random variables.
Prove the equivalence: $X_n \xrightarrow{P} 0 \iff \mathbb{E}[\min(1, |X_n|)] \to 0$.

response.text:
Let

\[
Y_n:=\min(1,|X_n|).
\]

Then \(0\le Y_n\le 1\), so \(\mathbb E[Y_n]\) is always well-defined.

We prove both directions.

---

## \((\Rightarrow)\) Suppose \(X_n \xrightarrow{P}0\)

By definition, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),

\[
\mathbb P(|X_n|>\varepsilon)\to 0.
\]

Fix \(0<\varepsilon<1\). We split according to whether \(|X_n|\le \varepsilon\) or \(|X_n|>\varepsilon\). Since \(\min(1,|X_n|)\le \varepsilon\) on \(\{|X_n|\le \varepsilon\}\), and \(\min(1,|X_n|)\le 1\) always, we have

\[
\min(1,|X_n|)
\le \varepsilon + \mathbf 1_{\{|X_n|>\varepsilon\}}.
\]

Taking expectations,

\[
\mathbb E[\min(1,|X_n|)]
\le \varepsilon + \mathbb P(|X_n|>\varepsilon).
\]

Letting \(n\to\infty\), using convergence in probability,

\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\mathbb E[\min(1,|X_n|)]
\le \varepsilon.
\]

Since this holds for every \(0<\varepsilon<1\), letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow 0\) gives

\[
\mathbb E[\min(1,|X_n|)]\to 0.
\]

---

## \((\Leftarrow)\) Suppose \(\mathbb E[\min(1,|X_n|)]\to 0\)

We must show that for every \(\varepsilon>0\),

\[
\mathbb P(|X_n|>\varepsilon)\to 0.
\]

On the event \(\{|X_n|>\varepsilon\}\), we have

\[
\min(1,|X_n|)\ge \min(1,\varepsilon).
\]

Therefore,

\[
\min(1,\varepsilon)\mathbf 1_{\{|X_n|>\varepsilon\}}
\le \min(1,|X_n|).
\]

Taking expectations gives

\[
\min(1,\varepsilon)\mathbb P(|X_n|>\varepsilon)
\le \mathbb E[\min(1,|X_n|)].
\]

Since \(\min(1,\varepsilon)>0\), we obtain

\[
\mathbb P(|X_n|>\varepsilon)
\le
\frac{\mathbb E[\min(1,|X_n|)]}{\min(1,\varepsilon)}
\to 0.
\]

Thus \(X_n\xrightarrow{P}0\).

---

Hence,

\[
\boxed{
X_n \xrightarrow{P}0
\iff
\mathbb E[\min(1,|X_n|)]\to 0.
}
\]
